<reflection>
All mechanisms except M5 fit similarly well (NLL ~-21.5). The single dataset is not discriminating. M5 (two-substrate binding by catalyst) is notably worse. Need experiments that stress different mechanistic features.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To discriminate, I need to vary catalyst concentration significantly. Key discriminating features:
- Catalyst dimerization (M2, M3, M13): rate scales non-linearly with [cat]. M3 predicts rate scales with [cat]² at low [cat].
- Simple MM (M1) vs. deactivation (M9-M20): high catalyst should give complete conversion for M1 but stalling for irreversible deactivation.
- Higher [cat] with lower [S] amplifies the [cat]-order signature.

Propose high catalyst concentration and moderate substrate. If the rate/[cat] ratio is much higher than at 0.01, this indicates dimer catalyst species (M3 shows [cat]² dependence at low [cat]). If deactivation dominates (M9, M13, M20), we should see stalling.

Predictions for [cat]=0.05, [S]=1.0, [P]=0:
- M1, M4, M6-M8 (no deactivation): full conversion, rate roughly 5x faster
- M9, M13, M20 (irreversible cat deactivation): may still stall but at higher conversion
- M3 (dimer active): rate increase >5x (super-linear in cat)
- M2, M13 (dimer forms but inactive): rate increase <5x (sub-linear)
- M11, M14, M16, M18, M19 (catS/catS2 deactivation): still see stalling
</hypothesis>
